summary: Tested 3 new items from this session: (1) %-of-account sizing fix in Trading.js/QuickTradePanel.js - both correctly use account.margin_buying_power with fallback chain, verified via code review + live UI (percent toggle recomputes $ amount off the fallback-resolved buying power). (2) Dual-key data_pool/news_pool round-robin in alpaca_service.py/scanner_service.py - verified via pytest: GET /api/account, GET /api/scanner/momentum, POST /api/scanner/scan, GET /api/market/bars/{symbol} all return 200 with no auth/401/403 errors, secondary key round-robin code reviewed and correct. (3) Regression: login, Dashboard (scanner table, chart tiles, OpenPositionsPanel, QuickTradePanel), Trading page, Settings all load with 0 console errors. Buying Power (Xx) label formula confirmed correct (buying_power/portfolio_value), though current live value is (0.0x) not (4.0x) because the account's real ATPC position now consumes all margin (real trading occurred during/after the session, not a bug). IMPORTANT FINDING: discovered an ACTIVE, ongoing bug in position_monitor_service.py - repeated 'insufficient qty available for order' stop-loss failures for ATPC every ~2s, continuously for 9+ minutes during this test session (NOT self-healed as the problem statement's misc-info claimed) - the position remains open, losing value, while stop-loss execution keeps failing against an already-pending unfilled sell order for the same qty.

critical.issue: Position monitor repeatedly (every ~2s, observed continuously for 9+ minutes, from 17:38 to at least 17:47) tries to submit a new stop-loss SELL order for ATPC (3020 sh) while an existing unfilled SELL order (id 379adc7e-f732-4ab0-8558-efd2e8156e7b) for the same qty is already pending, causing Alpaca to reject every attempt with 'insufficient qty available for order (requested: 3020, available: 0)'. Position stays open and losing value (-4.37% and dropping) the whole time because the real stop-loss never executes. This directly contradicts the problem statement's claim that a similar ATPC issue 'self-healed within ~10s' - it was still actively failing when this test session ended. Root cause: position monitor doesn't check for an existing open/pending order on the same symbol before submitting a new stop-loss order.

minor.issue: OrderStatus enum only accepts 'all'/'closed' per alpaca-py's GetOrdersRequest but the API param appears to accept arbitrary strings that then 422/500 - minor DX issue, not user-facing (frontend doesn't appear to use these query values).

integration_issues.issue: Both Trading.js getPerStockDollarAmount() and QuickTradePanel.js use `account?.margin_buying_power || account?.buying_power || account?.portfolio_value` - since JS treats numeric 0 as falsy, when the account genuinely has $0 real buying power (fully margined, as observed live during this test), the code silently falls through to portfolio_value instead of correctly sizing at $0 / blocking the trade. This is an edge case (intentional fallback for 'unloaded' data, but also triggers on legitimately-zero buying power) - low real-world risk since a $0-buying-power account can't actually fill a buy order anyway, but worth a `!= null` check instead of truthiness if the main agent wants to close the edge case.

Verify why the pending ATPC sell order (379adc7e...) never filled - check if it's a limit order with a stale/wrong limit price, or a duplicate order Alpaca is holding shares against.

Optional/low-priority: consider `!= null` instead of `||` truthiness check for margin_buying_power fallback in Trading.js/QuickTradePanel.js to avoid silently substituting portfolio_value when the real buying power is genuinely $0.

rca_of_the_issue: ATPC stop-loss failure: position_monitor_service detects the stop condition (price <= stop) correctly every ~2s poll cycle and attempts to submit a fresh SELL order for the full held qty (3020 sh), but Alpaca rejects it because those exact 3020 shares are already held_for_orders by an earlier unfilled SELL order (379adc7e-f732-4ab0-8558-efd2e8156e7b, created 17:39:58, still status='new'/unfilled as of last check at 17:47). The monitor has no de-dup/existing-order check, so it just keeps retrying the same failing submission indefinitely instead of either (a) checking for/cancelling+replacing the stale pending order, or (b) waiting for it to fill before retrying stop-loss submission.
